headline: The agent platform — chat agents with role-based prompts, a tool registry, custom personas, admin and manager screens, and an in-app help assistant — is largely backed by code, with three items the review could not settle: agent security controls, the command approval workflow, and a planned skills/assets standardisation.
what_is_there: The code shows a working chat agent that switches behaviour by role, a central registry of tools that separates read-only actions from ones that write or run commands, user-defined agent personas saved per user, both an admin tab and a manager tab for creating and editing agents, a floating in-app help assistant, and an alerting path that emails an administrator when an agent action is blocked.
what_is_unclear: The review could not confirm the permission gates, command risk tiers and audit logging described for agent security, nor the approval step before an agent runs a command — the files that would hold that logic were not among those examined, and the one file named after the command ticket only handles persona directives in chat. The open ticket about turning agents and skills into reusable assets also could not be confirmed either way from what was seen.
suggested_action: Ask the team to point to where permission gating, command risk classification, audit logging and the run-command approval step live, so those three 'Release it' tickets can be checked directly.
